title: Plan 3-month DSA prep from a YouTube playlist
scenario: You bookmarked a 60-video DSA playlist on YouTube (Striver / NeetCode-style). Placement season starts in 3 months. You can put in 90 minutes a day on weekdays, 3 hours on weekends. Some videos are 10 mins, some are 45. You don't want to ‘watch all 60’, you want a sequenced plan with practice between videos and a checkpoint every 2 weeks. You also keep getting bored and giving up at week 4.
badPrompt: make me a 3-month DSA study plan from a youtube playlist
badOutput: Month 1: Watch arrays, strings, and basic algorithms videos. Month 2: Move to trees and graphs. Month 3: Practice problems and review. Spend 1-2 hours daily. Take breaks. Stay consistent.

hints.title: Anchor your time honestly
hints.body: ‘90 min weekdays, 3 hr weekends’ is more useful than ‘1-2 hrs/day’. AI plans your real schedule, not your aspirational one.

hints.title: Force checkpoints
hints.body: Demand a check-in every 2 weeks with a measurable signal, e.g., ‘can solve 3 medium array problems in 45 min’. Plans without checkpoints fail at week 4.

checks.tip: Frame the artifact, a sequenced plan, not a list.
Anchor the topic, DSA, in concrete terms.
Anchor the source, the actual 60-video playlist.
Reference your real time budget and the placement-season deadline.
Demand checkpoints every 2 weeks. Anchors progress.
Tell Claude about your week-4 dropout pattern, it can plan against it.
Demand practice between videos. Watching alone doesn't build DSA muscle.
Specify a week-by-week table, not prose.
Force a measurable signal per checkpoint, ‘can solve 3 medium problems’.

tipIfLow: Study plans from AI fail because they ignore your real schedule and give no checkpoints. The unlock is honest time budgets (90 min weekdays, not ‘1-2 hrs’), checkpoints with measurable signals, AND naming the dropout pattern (week 4) so the plan can route around it.
goldPrompt: You are a learning coach who's seen students give up at week 4. I'm Aryan, 2nd-year B.Tech CSE. I have a 60-video Striver-style DSA playlist and 3 months until placements. Real schedule: 90 min weekdays, 3 hrs weekends. I drop off at week 4 from boredom. Output a 12-week plan with: (a) sequenced video clusters (not one-by-one), (b) practice problems between each cluster, (c) a measurable checkpoint every 2 weeks (e.g., 'solve 3 medium array problems in 45 min'), (d) one 'reset day' per fortnight to prevent burnout. Refuse to assume 8-hour days I don't have.
